nodes.label: Connected Stage Mission
nodes.rationale: Defines the purpose and scope of the Connected stage as a proof of concept to evolve the legacy tool lending application without changing business outcomes or moving authoritative data.

nodes.label: Rule Distribution
nodes.rationale: Rules are intentionally distributed across UI, native DLL, service, and database to demonstrate maintenance and scaling constraints; client and DLL checks improve feedback but are not authoritative; stored procedures are authoritative with row locks.

nodes.label: Legacy Shared Credential Model
nodes.rationale: Legacy desktop clients read a shared practice-level API key from a local or SMB file; key is sent as X-Api-Key; this models a migration liability, not a recommended design; must fail closed if missing or unreadable.

nodes.label: Application Service
nodes.rationale: AppServer is a self-hosted Web API 2 application that authenticates API calls, validates requests, supplies audit context, coordinates idempotent writes, maps database failures to HTTP responses, and owns all database access.

nodes.label: Checkout Request Flow
nodes.rationale: Illustrates duplicated rules, security boundary, idempotency behavior, and transaction boundary across UI, DLL, API, repository, and database.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL database contains bootstrap, schema, stored procedures, seed, reset, and test scripts; owns concurrency-sensitive decisions and durable state changes; stored procedures lock rows and write business and audit records in the same transaction.

nodes.label: Desktop Client
nodes.rationale: Desktop client is the Win32 executable that validates input, shows generated IDs, invokes native eligibility checks, and calls the service with WinHTTP; it never connects directly to PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Native Rules Library
nodes.rationale: NativeRules is an x86 DLL that calculates tier checkout limits, maximum loan durations, and checkout eligibility; provides immediate user feedback but is not authoritative.
